prerequisites: The basic knowledge of mechanics, structure and strength.

learning_outcomes.text: Make students familiar with the basics of theoretical and practical aircraft aerodynamics.
Acquire basic knowledge of airworthiness requirements and strength calculations of main aircraft parts.
Be able to make a proper choice as for the conception, structure and material for the aircraft design.
Determine the basic aerodynamic parameters, flight operation and flight characteristics of a typical aircraft.
Consider the structural design from the point of view of the strength and airworthiness requirements.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Historical overview of aviation development. Division of aircraft. Terminology. Airplane requirements.
Coordinate systems, load on aircraft. Maneuver, gust, load factor.
Theoretic. atmosphere. Physical properties of the atmosphere. International standard atmosphere.

Wrapping of bodies. Origin of aerodynamic forces and moments. Aerodyn. Characteristics of profiles, wings and aircraft. Influence of viscosity and compressibility of air Flight performance and properties. Stability and controllability.
Wing structures.
Spar structures, calculations.
Fuselage, cabin, tail units.
Landing gear, propulsion system.
Airborne systems of aircraft, classification, purpose, requirements.
Introduction to aircraft electrical onboard systems, introduction to control systems.
Introduction to aircraft instrumentation (classification, use). Principles of basic aerometric instruments. Other used physical principles in aircraft instruments.
Introduction to aircraft instrumentation. Electronic avionics system. Examples of cabins of modern aircraft of various categories.
Conception of aircraft, classification, statistical analysis of dependencies.
Calculation of maneuver and gust loads.
Bernoullis eq., airspeed measurements.
Example of measurements in the wind tunnel.
Aerodynamic characteristics of airfoils.
Calculation of forces and moments imposed on the simple wing.
Stress analysis of simple spar.
Critical stress definition for compression and shear.
Load capability of spar structure.
Requirements of aviation regulations for airborne systems.
Requirements of aviation regulations for electrical on-board and control systems.
Aircraft instrumentation requirements.
Instrumentation design for airplanes of various categories.

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theoretical part and practical exercises)

assessment_rules: Conditions for obtaining the course-unit credit include participation in the course (80% at the minimum). The essential exam is written (theoretical part and practical exercises), followed by oral verification. Lectures and seminars are compulsory, with attendance (80% at the minimum) recorded. Individual assignments must be finished and handed in by the credit week at the latest.
